spots.name: Karlatornet

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Karlatornet is a mixed-use skyscraper built by Serneke in Lindholmen in Gothenburg, Sweden. Started in 2019 and topped out in June 2023, the tower stands at 246 m (807 ft) tall with 74 floors, was completed in the autumn of 2024 and is the current tallest building in Sweden.

spots.name: Liseberg
spots.summary: Liseberg is an amusement park located in Gothenburg, Sweden, that opened in 1923. It is the second most visited theme park in Scandinavia, with around three million visitors annually.

spots.name: Götaplatsen
spots.summary: Götaplatsen is a public square in Gothenburg, Sweden, at the southern end of Avenyn, the city's main boulevard. The square was inaugurated when Gothenburg held a major international industrial exhibition, in 1923, celebrating the city's 300th anniversary.

spots.name: Gothenburg Museum of Art
spots.summary: The Gothenburg Museum of Art is an art museum located in the city of Gothenburg, Sweden. The collection consists of more than 70,000 works in total, most of which are Nordic art from the 15th century until today.

spots.name: Gothenburg Central Station
spots.summary: Gothenburg Central Station is the main railway station of Gothenburg and it is the oldest railway station in Sweden still in use. The station serves 27 million passengers per year, making it the second largest railway station in Sweden after Stockholm Central Station which it predates by 13 years.

spots.name: Gothenburg Botanical Garden
spots.summary: The Gothenburg Botanical Garden is located in Gothenburg, Sweden, and is one of the larger botanical gardens in Europe.

spots.name: Gothenburg Cathedral
spots.summary: Gothenburg Cathedral is a cathedral in Gothenburg, the second largest city in Sweden. It is the seat of the bishop of the diocese of Gothenburg in the Church of Sweden.

spots.name: Älvsborg Bridge
spots.summary: The Älvsborg Bridge is a suspension bridge over Göta älv in Gothenburg, Sweden, connecting the island of Hisingen with the mainland. It was designed by Sven Olof Asplund, and inaugurated on 8 November 1966 by Swedish communication minister Olof Palme.

spots.name: HSwMS Småland

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: HSwMS Småland (J19) is a Swedish Halland-class destroyer. She and HSwMS Halland were the only ones built of their class. Two more ships were ordered but they were never completed.

spots.name: Gustaf Adolfs torg
spots.summary: Gustaf Adolfs torg is a town square located in central Gothenburg, Sweden. It was named Stortorget until 1854 when a statue of the founding father of Gothenburg, king Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden was raised.

spots.name: German Church
spots.summary: The German Church, also called Christinae Church, is church located in the city centre of Gothenburg, Sweden. Named after Queen Christina, it was inaugurated in 1748, and used by the German and Dutch congregation in Gothenburg. The church contains a 42-bell carillon, which was cast by the Bergholtz Bellfoundry in 1961.

spots.name: Helix
spots.summary: Helix is a steel roller coaster located at Liseberg in Gothenburg, Sweden. The ride, built by Mack Rides, features two linear synchronous motor launches and has a top speed of 100 km/h. It features a 41-metre-tall (135 ft) dual-launch helix. The ride opened on 26 April 2014, Liseberg's opening date for the 2014 season.

spots.name: Gunnebo House
spots.summary: Gunnebo House is a mansion located outside Gothenburg, in Mölndal Municipality, Sweden. The main building, the garden facilities, the park and a larger outdoor area, were registered as a building monument and protected as a nature reserve in 1949.

spots.name: Oscar Fredrik Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Oscar Fredrik Church is a church in Olivedal in Gothenburg, Sweden. It was drawn by Helgo Zetterwall and erected in the 1890s. Belonging to the Gothenburg Oscar Fredrik Parish of the Church of Sweden, it was inaugurated on Easter Sunday, Sunday, 2 April 1893.

spots.name: AtmosFear
spots.summary: AtmosFear is a 116-metre-tall (381 ft) drop tower located in Liseberg amusement park in Gothenburg, Sweden, and is the second tallest drop tower in Europe, after Highlander at Hansa Park. AtmosFear is designed by Intamin and drops riders from a height of 100 metres (330 ft).

spots.name: Gothenburg City Hall
spots.summary: The Gothenburg City Hall is located in Gothenburg, Sweden. It was designed in the Beaux-Arts style and was used primarily as a law court until 2010.

spots.name: Feskekôrka
spots.summary: Feskekörka is a building in Gothenburg, Sweden, that formerly housed an indoor fish market. Its name is based on the building's resemblance to a neo-Gothic church. It opened on 1 November 1874, and was designed by the city architect Victor von Gegerfelt.

spots.name: Universeum

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Universeum is a public science centre, zoo and public aquarium in Gothenburg, Sweden that opened in 2001.

spots.name: Museum of Gothenburg
spots.summary: The Museum of Gothenburg is a local history museum located in the city centre of Gothenburg in western Sweden. It is located in the East India House, originally built as the Swedish East India Company offices in 1762. The city museum was established in 1861.

spots.name: Masthugg Church
spots.summary: Masthugg Church in Gothenburg, Sweden, was built in 1914. Its position on a high hill (Masthugget) close to the city and near the Göta älv makes it a striking sight – the church tower is 60 m (200 ft) high in itself.

spots.name: Skansen Kronan
spots.summary: Skansen Kronan is a redoubt on the hill Risåsberget, in the Haga district of Gothenburg, Sweden.

spots.name: Brunnsparken
spots.summary: Brunnsparken is a central square in Gothenburg, Sweden. It is located between Nordstan and Arkaden, and between two of Gothenburg's oldest streets, Norra Hamngatan and Södra Hamngatan. With its central location "Inom Vallgraven" and with numerous shopping centres it is a popular meeting place in Gothenburg.

spots.name: Kronhuset
spots.summary: Kronhuset, formerly known as Giötheborgz Tyghuhs, is a redbrick building in Västra Nordstaden in Gothenburg. It was constructed during the years 1643–1654 in a Dutch style, and is Gothenburg's joint-oldest secular building along with the Torstenson Palace.

spots.name: Järntorget
spots.summary: Järntorget is a public square in Gothenburg, Sweden. A hub for public transport, it is located west of Haga and is the starting point for the boulevards of Linnégatan to the south and Nya Allén to the east; and the streets of Första Långgatan and Andra Långgatan to the west.

spots.name: Equestrian statue of Charles IX in Gothenburg
Trädgårdsföreningen
spots.summary: The Garden Society of Gothenburg is a park and horticultural garden in central Gothenburg, Sweden. It is located next to Kungsportsavenyen and the Gamla Ullevi stadium.

spots.name: Kungsportsplatsen
spots.summary: Kungsportsplatsen is a square in the city centre of Gothenburg, Sweden. The square was constructed in 1852 and got its name after the King's Gate. The gate was the main entrance to the fortified city, which was and still is surrounded by a moat.

spots.name: Kungsportsavenyen
spots.summary: Avenyn, formally Kungsportsavenyen, is the main boulevard of Gothenburg, Sweden.

spots.name: Såningskvinnan
spots.summary: Såningskvinnan, popularly known as Johanna i Brunnsparken, is a statue of a standing woman in Gothenburg, Sweden, sculpted by Per Hasselberg in 1883. The original gypsum version of the statue remains at the Medicinal history museum of Gothenburg.

spots.name: HSwMS Sölve

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: HSwMS Sölve is one of seven Hildur-class monitors built for the Swedish Navy in the mid-1870s. The ship had an uneventful career and was sold in 1919 for conversion into a barge. She became a museum ship in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 1992.

spots.name: Maritiman

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Maritiman is a floating maritime museum located in Gothenburg, Sweden. The exhibition ships is currently anchored at Packhuskajen on the Göta River. It is the largest floating museum in the world. The Maritiman is a member of the Swedish Military Heritage Secretariat.

spots.name: Old Älvsborg
spots.summary: Älvsborg, now generally known as Old Älvsborg or Älvsborg Castle to distinguish it from the later New Älvsborg and Älvsborg Fortress, was a medieval castle situated on the rocky outcrop known as Klippan, on the south bank of the Göta Älv river within the urban area of the modern city of Gothenburg.

spots.name: Röhsska Museum
spots.summary: The Röhsska Museum, also known as Design Museum, is located in Gothenburg, Sweden. It is a museum focused on design, fashion and applied arts.

spots.name: Balder
spots.summary: Balder is a wooden roller coaster at the Liseberg amusement park in Gothenburg, Sweden. It opened in 2003 and was an instant success.

spots.name: Göteborgsoperan
spots.summary: The Gothenburg opera house is an opera house at Lilla Bommen in Gothenburg, Sweden. The Artistic Director for opera is Henning Ruhe since 2019, while Katrín Hall leads the Gothenburg Opera Dance Company.

spots.name: Museum of World Culture
spots.summary: The National Museum of World Culture opened in Gothenburg, Sweden, in 2004. It is a part of the public authority Swedish National Museums of World Cultures and builds on the collections of the former Göteborgs Etnografiska Museum that closed down in the year 2000.

spots.name: Gothenburg City Theatre
spots.summary: Gothenburg City Theatre opened in 1934 at Götaplatsen square in Gothenburg, Sweden. The theatre was designed by Swedish architect Carl Bergsten who gave the exterior a Neo-Classical look with a touch of Streamline Moderne.

spots.name: Hisingsbron
spots.summary: Hisingsbron is a vertical-lift bridge in central Gothenburg, Sweden, connecting the island of Hisingen to the mainland. The bridge was constructed between 2017 and 2021, replacing the Götaälvbro, and was inaugurated on 5 September 2021 by King Carl XVI Gustaf.

spots.name: Stora Teatern
spots.summary: Stora Teatern is a musical theater in the Lorensberg district of Gothenburg, Sweden. Inaugurated in 1859, it is situated in Kungsparken park south of Kungsportsplatsen.

photo.author: This image was produced by me, David Castor (user:dcastor). The pictures I submi

spots.name: Bourse
spots.summary: The Bourse is a municipal building in Gothenburg, western Sweden. It is located on the north side of Gustaf Adolf Square.

spots.name: Lisebergbanan
spots.summary: Lisebergbanan is a steel roller coaster at the Liseberg amusement park in Gothenburg, Sweden. It opened in 1987.

photo.author: The original uploader was WillMcC at English Wikipedia.

spots.name: Götaälvbron
spots.summary: Götaälvbron was a bascule bridge in central Gothenburg, Sweden, carrying normal road vehicles and trams. The bridge was constructed in 1937 to 1939 and in 1966 it was widened. It was closed for decommissioning in June 2021.

photo.author: Martin Olsson (mnemo on en/sv wikipedia and commons, martin@minimum.se).

spots.name: Torstenson Palace
spots.summary: The Torstenson Palace is a building on Södra Hamngatan in Gothenburg, also known as Kungshuset because it was formerly the Swedish king's residence in Gothenburg. It is currently the residence and offices of the landshövding of Västra Götaland County.

spots.name: Bältespännarparken
spots.summary: Bältespännarparken (Swedish: [ˈbɛ̂ltɛˌspɛnːarpaɾkɛn] is a section of Kungsparken in central Gothenburg, Sweden.

spots.name: Korsvägen
spots.summary: Korsvägen is a public square and transport hub in the events district of Gothenburg, Sweden.

spots.name: Gothenburg Concert Hall
spots.summary: Gothenburg Concert Hall is a concert hall located in Gothenburg, Sweden, built in 1935. The architect for the facility was Nils Einar Ericsson, a major advocate of Functionalism.

spots.name: Göteborgs Konsthall
spots.summary: Göteborgs Konsthall is a contemporary art exhibition hall in Gothenburg, Sweden.

spots.name: Haga Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Haga Church is a church building located in Gothenburg, Sweden. Belonging to the Gothenburg Haga Parish within the Diocese of Gothenburg of the Church of Sweden, it was opened on Advent Sunday, 27 November 1859.

spots.name: Järntorgsbrunnen
spots.summary: Järntorgsbrunnen, or using the artist's title, De fem världsdelarna, is a sculpture by Tore Strindberg, inaugurated October 12, 1927, at Järntorget, Göteborg, Sweden.

spots.name: Gothenburg Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Gothenburg Synagogue is a Conservative Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at Östra Larmgatan 12, near Drottningtorget, Gothenburg, in the municipality of Gothenburg, in the Västra Götaland County of Sweden.

spots.name: Skansen Lejonet
spots.summary: Skansen Lejonet, formally Westgötha Leijon, is a redoubt on the hill Gullberg in Gothenburg, Sweden, built in 1687–92 on the site of an earlier medieval castle. It was decommissioned in 1822 and has since served a range of other purposes.

spots.name: Gothenburg Natural History Museum
spots.summary: The oldest museum in Gothenburg includes a stuffed blue whale and is situated in Slottsskogen. Here you can learn about the history of animals from around the world. Among other things, they have a permanent exhibition dedicated to whales.

spots.name: Skanskaskrapan
spots.summary: Informally called "the lipstick" by the local, it features a viewing platform (Götheborgsutkiken) at 86 metres, which offers great views over the city.
